documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Annual.

PTSD: still in weekly therapy, a year and a bit out from last summer's crash. Psychiatry saw her in December. Flashbacks less often than last fall but still there; she does not drive and plans her walks and rides around that intersection. Stays alert to traffic constantly, doesn't sleep well on school nights. Says teaching is the part of the day that feels normal. No SI. No alcohol.

No headaches. Allergies were mild this year.

Meds: none. Allergies: NKDA.

Exam: vitals per flowsheet. Well appearing. HEENT normal. Neck no nodes. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft. Extremities no edema. Neuro nonfocal. Mood mildly anxious, affect full.

A/P
1. PTSD: chronic, followed by psychiatry with weekly therapy. Next psychiatry visit January.
2. History of mild TBI, remote femur ORIF: no issues.
3. Allergic rhinitis: seasonal, no treatment.
4. Health maintenance: flu today; updated COVID vaccine at pharmacy. Pap 2022 normal. Labs next year.

RTC 1 year.

documents.title: Psychiatry Follow-up
documents.author: psychiatry
documents.body:
Outpatient Psychiatry, follow-up
Date of service: 01/09/2024
Re: Abigail Whitcomb, DOB 09/01/1987, age 36
Allergies: NKDA. Current medications: none.

Interval history: 36-year-old teacher with PTSD tied to a 2020 collision, a 2021 armed robbery and the June 2022 crash in which she was a passenger and her friend was killed. Symptoms persist. She continues to have flashbacks of the 2022 crash, avoids the site and still does not drive. She is hypervigilant and feels on edge most of the time, finds it hard to stay focused at work, and has ongoing insomnia. Continues weekly therapy. No SI, no substance use, no alcohol.

Vital signs within normal limits.
Exam notable for a heightened startle response (jumped when a cart was wheeled past the door).
Mental status: cooperative, anxious affect, goal-directed, no SI/HI, no psychotic features.

Assessment: Post-traumatic stress disorder, chronic, ongoing symptoms.

Plan:
- Continue trauma-focused psychotherapy weekly.
- Sleep hygiene reviewed.
- Return in about a year.

Outpatient Psychiatry
